approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules and forms a fresh offspring pool for each batch. A frozen TabICLv2 model conditions on the current session archive, removes training-constant fingerprint columns, and supplies eight-view native score quantiles. The exact integral of each bounded-tail quantile curve ranks candidates for the inherited stall mask. Correlated Gaussian draws from the original count-fingerprint GP are converted to uniforms and then through those native quantile curves; sequential maxima receive the paid evaluations. Accepted scores update the same archive and breeding population.
approach.novelty: Replace only the location of each native predictive distribution with the original GP mean by an exact translation. Keep its centered spread, asymmetry, tails and dependence intact. This tests whether the weaker native location wastes valuable choices even when its distributional predictions look better. There are no completed same-Parent siblings in this request; the separately scheduled feature-visibility sibling changes the removed coordinates and retains native location, whereas this child retains the native feature filter and changes location. Their interaction is untested.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is weak value-directed allocation under the Parent native marginal location. All three actual summary/run pairs for n-16b934239c55 complete successfully: macro mean 0.47377281306454333, population SD 0.03865070499495466, seed macros 0.501270943666727, 0.500934688903316 and 0.419112806623587. Against formal Anchor/code ancestor n-cf8d309c06de the complete mean difference is -0.13325750314658766, with all three seed macros and twelve of fifteen endpoints lower. The published analysis and our exact trajectory/paid-log joins expose all 435 native batches and all 4350 paid proposals. This is an observed location weakness conditional on the purchased stream, not proof that location caused the endpoint loss. Reconstructed positive child-minus-best-generating-parent mass is 11.1890641226236 across all 4350 proposals, from 653 positive margins; the last 2175 proposals contribute 4.943625601057767 from 246 positive margins. hypothesis: Modify only the native marginal-location consumer of code Parent n-16b934239c55. For each candidate i, retain its inherited monotone piecewise-linear quantile curve Qnative_i on alpha=j/1000, j=1..999, with constant tails outside [.001,.999]. Let m_i be its exact inherited bounded-tail integral and let mu_GP_i be the ORIGINAL raw-score count-GP posterior mean computed on the same chronological accepted archive and candidate counts. Set delta_i=mu_GP_i-m_i and Qstar_i(u)=Qnative_i(u)+delta_i. Feed mu_GP_i directly to the unchanged stall-mask ranking and feed Qstar_i(Phi(z_i)) to the unchanged sequential first-index sampled maxima, using the same original jittered GP factor, normal block, row standardization and uniforms. The exact centered residual law Qstar_i-mu_GP_i equals Qnative_i-m_i. This is a deterministic location substitution within the quantile-copula recipe, with no variance rescaling, mean blend, clipping, Gaussian residual addition, feature repair or acquisition change. The causal prediction is that altered eligible/paid choices enter real feedback and increase complete-panel summed positive actual score-minus-best-generating-parent gain; endpoint gain is a separate question.

finding_summary.headline: GP-location translation raises useful paid gain and Parent endpoints, but late progress weakens and the Anchor target is unmet
finding_summary.insights: Native location was a consequential weakness on this retained quantile-residual host: replacing that consumer improved the registered aggregate gain and endpoints without changing centered uncertainty or dependence. The two borrowed elements actually operated—native quantile prediction and Gaussian-copula transport—but their translated combination remains an experimental hybrid. Its benefit neither validates native uncertainty against the original full Gaussian law nor transfers calibration claims from the literature. Better overall ordering, worse pinball loss and weaker late gains separate acquisition usefulness from predictive fit; rank equality with the GP is only an implementation identity. The positive aggregate does not establish ranking as the causal mediator or a uniform task/seed benefit. The remaining limitation is more specific than a failure to generate varied graphs: the chemistry audit found 1,951 typed scaffolds, yet each task's 30 highest-score molecules occupied only 2 to 14 cores, with peripheral variants sometimes tying. Smaller leading amine/aromatic and fluorinated ring systems accompany the strongest endpoint gains, while unusual ring geometry, reactive attachments and undefined stereochemistry persist. Together with the decline in late incumbent progress, this supports a diagnosis of limited productive core coverage during late refinement; a proposal operator or search scheme that can change core connectivity and ring geometry is the kind of intervention that could address that limitation. Its benefit is untested. The result settles this location substitution on this panel; the remaining residual-law contribution, late-search limitation, task safety and broader approach remain open.
finding_summary.results: The location substitution executed in all 435 batches, preserving the centered quantile law and copula within the registered numerical tolerance. Every selected batch differed from the same-state native replay: 2,608 of 4,350 paid identities were absent from its selected set. All 4,200 nonfinal purchases reached both models at the next fit; 2,521 of those were active-only identities. The primary complete-panel quantity, summed positive score gain over actual generating parents, rose from 11.189064 to 14.212984 (+3.023920), with 673 positive margins versus 653. This confirms the registered finite-panel useful-location prediction, although only 7 of 15 task/seed gain totals improved. The late half moved the other way: gain mass fell from 4.943626 to 4.445968 despite its positive-margin count rising from 246 to 259. Full incumbent gain rose from 3.979211 to 5.257451, while late incumbent gain fell from 1.763311 to 1.090316. Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.473773 to 0.558989 (+0.085216), all three seed macros improved, and 10 of 15 task endpoints increased. The new mean is still 0.048041 below the formal Anchor, so its separate +0.002 criterion is unmet; protocol task safety cannot be assessed from the supplied margins/decision. On the same purchased labels, translated versus native ordering accuracy was 0.711366 versus 0.700221 overall and 0.735066 versus 0.735695 late. Translated pinball loss was worse (0.020238 versus 0.019020); 90% coverage fell from 0.785977 to 0.763908 with identical widths. There was no technical failure or fallback.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heterocycles, amine cages and fluorinated fused systems; undefined stereochemistry and reactive attachments persist
molecular.overall_character: This assessment covers all authorized Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 for n-e2506e11f536 and published code Parent n-16b934239c55. Both Child evaluation and Parent pairing are complete in context.comparison; all supplied Child and Parent trajectory files exist. Each node supplies 4500 accepted records, including 4350 optimizer molecules; the chemistry of rejected proposals is not available here. The Child is a mixture of substituted indoles and lactams, extended aza-aromatic assemblies, phenolic amine cages, enlarged nitrogen rings, and fluorinated partially saturated heterocycles. Across accepted optimizer molecules its heavy-atom minimum/median/maximum is 1/30/120, versus 4/35/120 in the Parent. Ring-rich and aromatic-rich describe the output accurately: the digest ring-closure incidence ranges from 0.9851 to 1.0, while aromatic-text incidence ranges from 0.7437 to 0.9954. Those are molecule-level string flags, not fractions of atoms. There are ordinary medicinal-chemistry fragments, including amines, carbonyls, ethers and phenols, but many occur inside unusually fused, bridged or extensively repeated scaffolds. RDKit structural audits find N-halogen bonds in 704 Child molecules versus 334 Parent molecules, O-halogen bonds in 161 versus 75, O-O bonds in 71 versus 396, and carbon-carbon cumulated double bonds in 119 versus 17. These flags motivate chemical review; they do not measure stability, synthesis success or toxicity. The Child has 2574 molecules with unassigned perceived tetrahedral centers, no assigned centers and no formally charged atoms. Neutral amines are visibly present, so absence of charge notation must not be misread as absence of ionizable chemistry. There are 1951 typed and 1305 generic Murcko scaffolds across the Child output, but the 30 highest-score molecules within each task contain only 2 to 14 typed scaffolds. Thus graph variation is substantial while productive families within individual sessions can be narrow. Apparent synthetic plausibility and drug-likeness are qualitative readings; no synthesis, conformational strain, pKa, assay or binding-pose evidence was supplied. Parent differences are descriptive associations under this panel, not attribution to an algorithm component. No unobserved target motif can be identified from these trajectories alone. Descriptor and provenance evidence: policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/pooled-descriptors.json; policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/source-manifest.json.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 accepted optimizer molecules have 2 to 48 heavy atoms, median 24, and usually combine several aromatic rings with an amide or lactam. Seed 0 retains a substituted indole carboxamide with methoxy, methyl, aminomethyl and aryl-halogen decoration; its highest-score molecule also has an N-fluoroamide. Seed 1 instead reaches an ethoxyphenyl/halopyridyl substituted bicyclic N-N lactam, while seed 2 reaches a fused polycyclic lactam with ether and alkyl substituents. The 30 highest-score molecules occupy 23 to 26 heavy atoms and seven typed scaffolds. This is not an absence of rings or carbonyl chemistry. Compared with the Parent, the median size is similar (24 versus 25 heavy atoms), while the Child includes more partially saturated bicyclic chemistry; the Parent seed leaders are mainly aza-aromatic ketone or indole carboxamide relatives. The Child seed leaders score 0.44989726212142783, 0.4454539912731944 and 0.43554057891621306; corresponding Parent leaders score 0.4711064141789182, 0.46092619585962435 and 0.42762099872850584. The polycyclic and N-N-containing leaders require a more demanding synthetic and stereochemical assessment than their familiar aryl, ether and amide fragments alone suggest; 262 molecules have unassigned perceived centers.
missing_features: Consistent retention of compact, coherent carbonyl-bearing ring systems across proposals is missing; the low-score tail includes scaffold duplication and complete fragmentation.

Well-supported ordinary attachment and stereochemical alternatives around the higher-score cores are not established: N-fluoroamides remain among leaders and the bicyclic structures carry no assigned configuration. The trajectories do not establish a missing target-specific pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial substituted indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. Compact elaborations reach 0.44989726212142783, whereas a 48-heavy-atom peroxide-linked duplication scores 9.399013328085669e-15 and the isolated F-F proposal scores 0.0. The visible gradient favors a coherent compact heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement over either scaffold duplication or loss of the scaffold. It does not identify a universal favorable halogen: the closely related halopyridyl Br, Cl and F variants in seed 1 share 0.42749549733373915. The final seed-2 thioether/alkyl variant scores 0.1312472037266703 despite retaining its ring system, so ring count alone does not explain the scores.

missing_features: The output lacks assigned configurations for the stereogenic amine cages and does not express formal protonation alternatives; 862 molecules have unassigned perceived centers. The supplied scores cannot establish which configurations or charge states would help.

The scored high-value amine/aromatic arrangements are not consistently realized in ordinary, less geometrically demanding ring systems. Basic amine capability itself is visibly present and should not be described as missing.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The small aryl sulfonate scores 0.00024675866379847753 and an N-chloroamide/N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine scores 0.00016650955053713697, while compact ring systems with exposed secondary or tertiary amine centers and aromatic/phenolic groups reach 0.994627130457666. All 30 highest-score molecules carry the audited neutral nonaromatic single-bonded N motif, but that flag is not a pKa measurement. Nor is any amine sufficient: the final seed-0 aryl hydrazine fragment scores 0.007492990139775072. The association concerns the complete amine/aromatic geometry, not a standalone nitrogen count, and the trajectory does not establish a binding pose or biological potency.

per_task.generated_character: The output is dominated by fused aromatic heterocycles and enlarged nitrogen-containing rings bearing carbonyls, N-methyl groups, alkyl-substituted aryl groups and ethers. Accepted optimizer structures range from 1 to 67 heavy atoms, median 32. The highest-score seed-0 example has 33 heavy atoms: a propyl/ethoxy aryl substituent on an indole-like core joined to an enlarged ketone/lactam/tertiary-amine ring. Seed 1 favors a more extensively fused aza-aromatic lactam; seed 2 retains an N-N-containing enlarged ring and pyridyl/phenyl substituents. The Parent also produces enlarged nitrogen rings and aromatic/carbonyl combinations, with median 35 heavy atoms. Child seed leaders score 0.2363146341487732, 0.22344648696506328 and 0.2121823339838681; the Parent values are 0.2225098886497406, 0.2133584675546675 and 0.22020415990760814. These are different arrangements of related chemical ingredients, not evidence that the Child has discovered a missing functional-group class. Evidence files (relative to runs/SPIRAL2): policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/sources/child/seed-0/trajectories/median_2.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/sources/child/seed-1/trajectories/median_2.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/sources/child/seed-2/trajectories/median_2.jsonl; nodes/n-16b934239c55/seed-0/trajectories/median_2.jsonl; nodes/n-16b934239c55/seed-1/trajectories/median_2.jsonl; nodes/n-16b934239c55/seed-2/trajectories/median_2.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-median_2.json; policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-median_2.json; policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-median_2.json.
liabilities: Enlarged lactam/amine rings and unusual N-N linkages require explicit synthetic and conformational justification. Familiar functional groups do not establish a practical route to these fused architectures.

There are 14 molecules with at most six heavy atoms and nine with at least 60, plus ten with a perceived entirely aromatic ring of four or fewer atoms. These are descriptive boundary cases, not a universal molecular-size rule.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of useful aromatic/carbonyl connectivity during size and ring changes is missing; fragment-only and duplicated-scaffold proposals remain present.

Alternative successful arrangements are limited relative to the many generated graphs: the 30 highest-score molecules contain ten typed scaffolds from 397 over the full stream. Broader graph variation alone has not demonstrated broader high-score chemistry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted carbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. A retained aromatic/carbonyl core with an enlarged N-containing ring and propyl/ethoxy decoration reaches 0.2363146341487732; C, C=C and NNN score 0.0. A 61-heavy-atom duplicated carbonyl-heterocycle assembly scores 0.10842720406950315. The high cohort therefore favors a coherent arrangement over fragmentation or whole-scaffold duplication. It remains a modest local gradient: replacing a substituent on the seed-0 carbonyl ring with F or methyl gives the same 0.2339854106482522. The trajectories alone do not identify the unobserved structures behind the objective or justify a specific target scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: These structures are compact but architecturally unusual: 8 to 50 heavy atoms, median 28, with a median of five perceived rings. The seed-1 leader is a 30-heavy-atom, five-ring nonaromatic structure combining a fused cyclic urea/lactam-like dicarbonyl system, a cyclopropyl substituent, an imine-containing sulfur ring, alcohol, C-F and fluoromethyl groups. It has four unassigned perceived centers. Seed 0 retains a partially aromatic dicarbonyl heterocycle fused to an unsaturated amine ring and a fluorinated carbocycle; seed 2 produces imino aza-aromatics attached to a fluorinated cyclobutene and a bridged carbocycle bearing an acyl fluoride. Aromatic-text incidence is 0.7437, the lowest among these five outputs, while ring-closure incidence is 1.0. The Parent has the same median heavy-atom count, but fewer N-halogen-bearing molecules (114 versus 416) and no carbon allene motifs versus 108 in this Child stream. The Child seed leaders score 0.506913769157628, 0.6467462742507727 and 0.6166736435591553; Parent leaders score 0.4746557230814677, 0.21976588771462166 and 0.524911241687462. Evidence files (relative to runs/SPIRAL2): policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/sources/child/seed-0/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/sources/child/seed-1/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/sources/child/seed-2/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-16b934239c55/seed-0/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-16b934239c55/seed-1/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-16b934239c55/seed-2/trajectories/sitagliptin_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-sitagliptin_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-sitagliptin_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-sitagliptin_mpo.json.
liabilities: There are 416 N-halogen-bearing and 102 O-halogen-bearing molecules, and 108 with carbon-carbon cumulated double bonds. The acyl-fluoride and N-fluoro examples are chemically reactive motifs, not evidence of ordinary stable drug candidates.

There are 805 molecules with unassigned perceived centers. Dense small-ring fusion, sulfur-containing imines, enol-like alcohol substitution and multiple fluorinated centers make synthesis and three-dimensional plausibility uncertain without additional evidence.
missing_features: The output does not reliably combine its favored compact, fluorinated heterocyclic geometry with ordinary attachment chemistry: N-halogen motifs are prevalent even in the highest-score cohort, although the best observed molecule avoids them.

Assigned configurations and simpler, comparably scored alternatives to the heavily fused small-ring systems are not demonstrated. The trajectories do not establish a particular desired stereoisomer or charge state.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic carbonyl heterocycle scores 0.0020944534688323298, and a 50-heavy-atom scaffold assembly scores 3.5331505272531085e-35. Compact fluorinated nitrogen-containing polycycles reach 0.6467462742507727; the 30 highest-score molecules are 25 to 30 heavy atoms. Less aromatic, more saturated ring chemistry is visibly compatible with high scores here, but this is not a monotone fluorine-count rule. N-fluoro motifs occur in 26 of those 30 molecules, while the highest-score example has no N-halogen bond. The data show strong preferences among complete connectivity patterns and substituent combinations; they do not establish that reactive attachments are necessary or that a particular missing pharmacophore would close the remaining gap.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-e2506e11f536 accepted optimizer molecules under Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, with published n-16b934239c55 as the paired baseline. Structural audits find 704 N-halogen-bearing, 161 O-halogen-bearing and 119 carbon-allene-bearing molecules, compared with 334, 75 and 17 in the baseline. O-O-bearing molecules decrease from 396 to 71, so there is no uniform change in chemical liabilities. N-halogen attachments persist in some highest-score cohorts, but other leaders use ordinary amines and carbon-linked halogens. These are motif observations, not measured instability or an attributed component effect.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain ordinary local bonding environments while elaborating useful heterocyclic cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A general chemical editing capability would need to preserve useful ring and substituent arrangements while offering ordinary local-bonding alternatives. Attachment-atom context should remain distinguishable from whole-scaffold identity. Any change remains a conditional hypothesis to be assessed with current-session feedback; these structural associations do not justify a blanket motif ban or promise higher scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-e2506e11f536 on the complete supplied Search panel. None of its 4350 accepted optimizer molecules has an assigned perceived tetrahedral center or a formally charged atom, while 2574 have at least one unassigned perceived center. High-score examples include bridged tertiary amines and fluorinated fused rings. Published n-16b934239c55 also lacks assigned centers and formal charge notation. The structures show amines already exist; neither pKa nor a preferred stereoisomer is established.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks explicit stereochemical and ionization alternatives despite generating stereogenic, potentially ionizable ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation and generator would need to express chemically meaningful configuration and charge alternatives when applicable, while preserving canonical identity and using only current-session observations. This addresses missing representational coverage; it is not evidence that any specific configuration or protonation improves a score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: the same Child and paired baseline Search trajectories. The Child has 23 accepted optimizer molecules with at most six heavy atoms and 384 with at least 60, compared with one and 571 in the baseline. Several observed high-score families are compact connected heterocycles, while both disconnected-in-function tiny fragments and repeated large scaffold assemblies occur in their low-score tails. Those two descriptive size cutoffs summarize exposure; they are not inferred chemical acceptance limits. Other high-score families contain larger connected ring systems, so a universal size preference is unsupported.
transferable_gaps.gap: Scaffold elaboration does not consistently preserve useful connectivity across both fragmentation and excessive whole-scaffold growth.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: General graph edits would need to preserve alternative ring/linker arrangements at multiple sizes while maintaining chemically meaningful connectivity. Let current-session evidence determine which survive, and keep both size tails visible. The observations support neither a universal heavy-atom floor or ceiling nor attribution of the chemistry differences to a particular algorithm component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-e2506e11f536 Search trajectories. The full accepted optimizer stream contains 1951 typed Murcko scaffolds, but the separate 30-molecule highest-score cohorts contain only 2 to 14 typed scaffolds. Exact score ties occur among peripheral halogen or alkyl variants of the same core. Ring-rich output includes tight fusion, bridging and enlarged nitrogen rings, so access to rings is abundant; ordinary alternative geometries around the same useful chemical features are not consistently represented among leaders. This is a finite-panel association, not proof that scaffold novelty causes progress.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many distinct graphs do not consistently yield several chemically distinct productive core families within a session.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to retain access to substantive changes in core connectivity and ring geometry as well as peripheral analogues, distinguishing chemical-family coverage from string novelty. Use those descriptions as diagnostics conditioned on this output, not as target scaffolds, an imposed diversity reward or a component-credit claim.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
